why: Flaky test fix in today's tooling, test code only (0036), with one fix round. Cause: until() in scripts/typecheck.integration.test.ts bounded its polls by a Date.now() + 5 s deadline, and on CI run 43831921638 the runner's wall clock stepped forward, so the deadline ended in a test vitest timed at 37 ms. The first round blamed a slow node start, which was wrong; the review caught it from the run's own timing. Fix: until() now reads its deadline from performance.now(), the monotonic clock, with the same 5 s bound, which covers every poll in the file. named() also no longer polls for the stand-in compiler's start: the stand-in prints 'ready' on a pipe after it has written its name, named() awaits that line through the child's stdout event (and fails at once if the child errors or exits first), then checks pgrep -x once with the same assertion. No assertion was dropped.
note: The law file is .integration. and spawns processes, so it was not run on the laptop; the change was reasoned from the code. Ran pnpm format, pnpm lint and one pnpm typecheck. PR 1506 (the typecheck port) edits the same lines of named.mjs and named(), so the two conflict and the second to land takes the other's change.
